📡 Iran’s maritime transport remains active despite sanctions: Official

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Minister of Roads and Urban Development Farzaneh Sadegh has described maritime transport as an important manifestation of Iran’s economic and diplomatic strength.

In a message marking World Maritime Day on Wednesday, Sadegh said Iran’s coastlines represent an important part of the country’s national and economic strength, while maritime transport plays a key role in sustaining trade moving and developing the country’s maritime sector.
​
She added that the continued movement of goods is not merely an economic activity but also demonstrates that Iran’s vital economic routes remain active despite pressures and sanctions.
​
Sadegh also stressed the importance of regional cooperation in maintaining security and stability in the Persian Gulf, saying Iran remains committed to ensuring sustainable security in the strategic waterway and protecting the interests of regional nations.
​
The minister praised seafarers, maritime specialists, port workers, and others involved in the sector for their role in keeping Iran’s trade and economy moving.
​
World Maritime Day is observed annually on September 24, highlighting the importance of seafarers and the global maritime industry.

⚡️ Iran Army commander highlights maritime sector’s role in economic resilience

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Rear Admiral Habibollah Sayyari, deputy chief of the Iranian Army for Coordination, has highlighted the strategic importance of the maritime sector in ensuring the country’s economic resilience and supply chains.

In a message marking World Maritime Day, Sayyari said on Wednesday that the sea is a key pillar of national power, a driver of trade and the economy, and vital to energy security and the continuity of supply chains.
​
He said the US-Israeli wars imposed over the past year demonstrated the importance of Iran’s maritime capacity, noting that seafarers and those working in shipping, ports and energy transportation had ensured the continued flow of essential goods, raw materials, energy and other vital supplies.
​
Sayyari also highlighted the roles of the Islamic Republic of Iran Shipping Lines, the Ports and Maritime Organization, and the National Iranian Tanker Company in maintaining supply chains, maritime trade and the country’s economic interests.
​
He stressed that improving maritime safety and security, modernizing and developing fleets and infrastructure, protecting the marine environment and training specialized human resources were essential to forward-looking governance of the sector.
​
Sayyari said these measures could further strengthen Iran’s position in the regional and global maritime transport and blue economy networks.
